entries.description: Hidden instructions in pages, comments, docs or tool outputs that hijack an agent that reads them. The root cause of most other items; zero-click; any user-generated content on the site can carry it.
entries.name: Indirect prompt injection via content the agent reads
entries.note: Documented pattern; live detection needs content inspection of search queries and page text, not wired into this working model.

entries.description: An agent is steered by a poisoned MCP tool description before any tool is called; secrets smuggled in parameters. Reported success up to 72.8% in MCPTox research (exact counts disputed between paper versions — treat as indicative).
entries.name: Tool poisoning / poisoned MCP tool descriptions

entries.description: Theft leaves through benign-looking channels: public comments, Markdown image URLs, extra tool parameters. Destination + encoded payload are detectable.
entries.name: Exfiltration via benign channels

entries.description: Fake bot user-agents, generic Chrome user-agents, IPs outside published ranges, robots.txt ignored. The most documented website-facing deception; user-agent alone is not identity.
entries.name: Spoofed / stealth identity

entries.description: Read private data, then write/send it to a new destination. Catches exfiltration and scope abuse that tool allow-lists miss.
entries.name: Unsafe tool chaining / read-then-send sequences

entries.description: An agent has no business on /admin, internal APIs, metadata endpoints, localhost or secret files. High signal, low false-positive rate.
entries.name: Probing admin / internal / SSRF targets

entries.description: A previously benign agent or tool suddenly changes description, schema or call pattern. One-time approval is not a control; change detection is the only defence.
entries.name: Rug-pull / tool-definition change

entries.description: Environment dumps, SSH keys, bearer/API keys in outputs or parameters. One leaked token means full privilege; high-entropy strings are automatable to detect.
entries.name: Credential / token harvesting in agent traffic

entries.description: Chain depth, fan-out, cost per session exploding. A single request can fan out to thousands of calls; cost and availability impact even without theft.
entries.name: Agent-loop / fan-out storms and token-burning

entries.description: Tool mix, endpoints or data accessed diverge from the session's declared purpose. Catches goal hijack, memory poisoning and misaligned agents that otherwise look normal.
entries.name: Scope drift / rogue-agent behaviour

entries.description: An agent systematically probes paths, parameters and hidden APIs to build a map for a later attack. Signals: sequential path scanning, 404 bursts, unusual endpoint order.
entries.name: Endpoint mapping & enumeration

entries.description: Bulk harvesting of content, pricing, PII-shaped data or model-training data beyond any fair-use pattern. Signals: full-catalog traversal, download velocity, headless fingerprints.
entries.name: Scraping & exfiltration

entries.description: Hundreds of coordinated agents generating plausible, expensive requests that exhaust the origin. Signals: correlated fingerprints, synchronised bursts, costly-endpoint focus.
entries.name: Agent swarm / agentic DDoS
